acquisition_method.evidence: Mass spectrometry (MS) was acquired using a data-dependent top 10 method that dynamically chose the most abundant precursor ions from the survey scan (350–1200 m/z) for higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) fragmentation.

alkylation_concentration.evidence: Each sample, comprising 100 µg of proteins, was first reduced with 100 mM DTT for 5 minutes at 100°C and then alkylated with 100 mM iodoacetamide for 30 minutes in the dark.

alkylation_reagent.evidence: Each sample, comprising 100 µg of proteins, was first reduced with 100 mM DTT for 5 minutes at 100°C and then alkylated with 100 mM iodoacetamide for 30 minutes in the dark.

cleavage_agent.evidence: Subsequently, the protein suspensions underwent digestion with 4 µg of trypsin (Promega) in 40 µL of 50 mM NH4HCO3 buffer overnight at 37°C, and the resulting peptides were collected as a filtrate.

collision_energy.evidence: The normalized collision energy was set to 33%, and the dynamic exclusion for selected ions was set to 30 seconds.

instrument.evidence: The samples underwent chromatography using the Easy nLC system (Thermo Fisher Scientific, USA), followed by analysis with an Orbitrap Exploris 480 mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, USA).

labeling.evidence: An integrated analysis of RNA sequencing (RNA-seq)-based transcriptomics and label-free quantitative proteomics was performed in both normal and burned corneas.
